{"problem": {"theorem": "I have an \(n \times n\) sheet of stamps, from which I've been asked to tear out blocks of three adjacent stamps in a single row or column. (I can only tear along the perforations separating adjacent stamps, and each block must come out of the sheet in one piece.) Let \(b(n)\) be the smallest number of blocks I can tear out and make it impossible to tear out any more blocks. Prove that there are real constants \(c\) and \(d\) such that

\[
\frac{1}{7} n^{2}-c n \leq b(n) \leq \frac{1}{5} n^{2}+d n
\]

for all \(n>0\).", "assumptions": [], "domain": "usamo", "explicit_subgoals": []}, "target": {"node_id": "n2", "version": 2}, "target_node": {"text": "1.  Lower bound \(b(n)\ge \tfrac1{7}n^2-cn\).  
 
Fix any one of the \(b(n)\) removed blocks.  If it is a horizontal block occupying cells \((i,j),(i,j+1),(i,j+2)\), then it “hits’’ (i.e.\ destroys at least one cell of) at most
  •  all horizontal triples that include one of those three cells;  in a row of length \(n\), each interior cell lies in 3 horizontal triples and each end‐cell in 1 or 2, and one checks easily that the three consecutive cells \((i,j),(i,j+1),(i,j+2)\) together lie in at most 5 distinct horizontal triples;  
  •  all vertical triples that include one of those three cells;  each of the three removed stamps lies in at most 3 vertical triples, so altogether at most \(3\times3=9\) vertical triples.  
Hence that one horizontal block can destroy at most \(5+9=14\) of the \(T\) potential triples.  Likewise any vertical block destroys at most \(14\) potential triples.", "claim": "Bounds the number of potential triples hit by any single removed block by fourteen.", "scope": [], "depends_on": ["n1"], "goal_refs": []}, "closed_predecessors": [{"node_id": "n1", "version": 2, "claim": "Defines potential triples, correctly counts them for every positive integer n, including n=1, and states that every potential triple is hit in a blocked configuration.", "text": "Proof. We think of a final “blocked” configuration as the result of tearing out \(b(n)\) disjoint 3-stamp blocks, each lying in one row or one column, so that no further such block remains. Call any three consecutive positions in a row or column a “potential triple.” Each row contains \(\max\{n-2,0\}\) horizontal potential triples, and each column contains the same number of vertical potential triples. Hence
\[
H=V=n\max\{n-2,0\},\qquad T=2n\max\{n-2,0\}.
\]
In particular, these counts are zero when \(n=1\), and for \(n\ge2\) they equal \(H=V=n(n-2)\) and \(T=2n(n-2)\). Since the configuration is blocked, every potential triple must be hit, meaning that at least one of its stamps has been removed.", "scope": [], "depends_on": []}], "counterexample_search": true, "rule_candidates": [{"id": "grp_first_iso", "name": "First isomorphism theorem for groups", "statement": "If phi: G -> H is a group homomorphism, then G/ker(phi) is isomorphic to im(phi).", "conditions": ["phi is a group homomorphism", "ker(phi) is the kernel of phi"], "conclusion": "G/ker(phi) is isomorphic to im(phi).", "rule_digest": "335c687d26f64e41584f1b8bc575aec9d78223b01c4821bf0056bf8533de0c19", "applicability": "unchecked"}, {"id": "grp_normal_quotient", "name": "Quotient group criterion", "statement": "If N is a normal subgroup of G, then the set of left cosets G/N forms a group under (aN)(bN) = abN.", "conditions": ["N is a subgroup of G", "N is normal in G"], "conclusion": "G/N is a group and coset multiplication is well-defined.", "rule_digest": "f6d458aa2e7463efeea7a535cdbe0f0f7930259cfe7f845b5350ec03454da876", "applicability": "unchecked"}, {"id": "grp_subgroup_test", "name": "Subgroup test", "statement": "A nonempty subset H of a group G is a subgroup if for all a,b in H, ab^{-1} is in H.", "conditions": ["H is nonempty", "H is a subset of G", "G is a group"], "conclusion": "H is a subgroup of G.", "rule_digest": "ba2e60e3c051f1e20706af088d5f217ae14581272220bfc9f34a7f86eea0d4e8", "applicability": "unchecked"}]}
